description.narrative: Through the Malawi Governance for Solutions (GfS) Activity, USAID seeks to build on the incremental gains in decentralization and associated service delivery improvements, with the understanding that to make the significant leaps now required for Malawi to meet its own development goalsin the face of a fast-growing, young populationa bold, adaptive, and sustainable approach is required.

Recognizing that capable government systems are critical to sustainably deliver health services, USAID partners directly with the local governments in two Malawian districts through the U.S. Presidents Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and the U.S. Presidents Malaria Initiative (PMI). The partnerships with Mangochi and Zomba District Councils are helping local governments improve health outcomes as part of USAIDs government-to-government (G2G) model.

description.narrative: (Malawi): Tackling Serious and Organized Corruption (TSOC) supports Malawian law enforcement to increase the likelihood and severity of sanction for serious and organized corruption. This activity strengthens technical capacity and interagency coordination among key law enforcement agencies, including the Anti Corruption Bureau, Director of Public Prosecutions, Financial Intelligence Agency, and the Malawi Police Service, to detect, investigate, and prosecute strategic corruption cases..TSOC will increase the risks of engaging in corruption and strengthen systems that regulate the movement of money and services through the economy, by supporting efforts to publicly expose corrupt individuals and corporations; seize and recover assets linked to corruption and other serious crimes; as well as improve strategic case work and conviction rates. Working through embedded technical assistance, TSOC will increase the practical skills and working knowledge of law enforcement agencies, to address obstacles that impede effective prosecution of corruption and public fraud cases. The activity will also support a range of prevention activities that engage non-state actors, including media, civil society, and the private sector, to implement anti-corruption and accountability activities. These include investigative journalism, advocacy for greater transparency in the business environment, and advocacy for greater parliamentary scrutiny of government spending..TSOC contributes to Malawi's Integrated Country Strategy (ICS) Goal 1: Democratic and Accountable Governance; and Objective 1.1: Support Malawian institutions, including parliament, the judiciary, and accountability institutions, to make governance more effective, transparent, and accountable. It also supports the Mission's CDCS (2020 - 2025) Development Objective 1, which seeks to improve public sector effectiveness and accountability at the national and decentralized levels.

title.narrative: Government to Government (G2G) - Zomba District Council

description.narrative: (Malawi): In line with USAID's vision of system strengthening for greater sustainability and resilience, USAID/Malawi entered into a direct three-year Government-to-Government (G2G) agreement with the Zomba District Council (ZDC). This integrated health activity supports the implementation of maternal and child health; family planning and reproductive health; nutrition; tuberculosis and HIV services. FY 2021 funds will enable the ZDC to: 1) implement the family health package of services through integrated outreach visits; 2) procure essential equipment; 3) provide supportive supervision; and 4) strengthen on-the-job mentoring to promote quality of care at both facility and community levels. The activity will support the 151 priority health care workers and four support staff recruited for ZDC using the Government of Malawi's recruitment and salary payment systems. This activity is complemented by a separate USAID award to the Government of Malawi's Ministry of Finance to support salary payments for the health care workers and support staff workers until the Government of Malawi absorbs them within the three year award period. Direct G2G support to decentralized districts with strong political will, sufficient devolved authority, and an acceptable capacity level will enhance Malawi's pathway to locally led development through strengthened capacity and commitment of the government to build sustainable and resilient health systems; ensure long-term sustainability, increase efficiency, strengthen transparency, and promote accountability. This activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.2 - Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance and 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and are able to contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work..
Reduce the transmission and impact of HIV/AIDS through support for prevention, care and treatment programs.

title.narrative: Ministry of Finance: Human Resources for Health Salary Support Activity (Government-to Government)

description.narrative: (Malawi): The shortage and equitable distribution of well-trained, and highly skilled health care workers is the most significant barrier to ensuring universal health coverage and improving the health status of Malawians. In line with USAID's vision of systems strengthening for greater sustainability and resilience, USAID entered into a direct government to government agreement with two district councils (Zomba and Mangochi), to strengthen health systems. Given the pivotal role of human resources to obtain the expected outcomes, and the acute shortage of healthcare workers in the districts, USAID is providing direct funding to enable the Ministry of Finance pay the salaries of one hundred and fifty one health care workers and four support staff recruited under the Zomba District Council including two hundred and thirty one health care workers and one support staff for Mangochi District Council. At the end of the three-year period, the Government of Malawi will take over payment of salaries. Funding for the salaries passes through the national payroll system with USAID resources managed in a separate account. FY 2022 funds will enable the Ministry of Finance to continue to provide salary payment for health care workers and support staff recruited by the two District Councils. . ..This activity leverages PEPFAR funding, which has successfully transitioned U.S. government funded health care workers to the Government of Malawi. The use of the government's payroll systems generates commitment and accountability in support of locally led development..This activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.2 - Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance and 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and are able to contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work.

Funding for the salaries passes through the national payroll system with USAID resources managed in a separate account. FY 2022 funds will enable the Ministry of Finance to continue to provide salary payment for health care workers and support staff recruited by the two District Councils. . ..This activity leverages PEPFAR funding, which has successfully transitioned U.S. government funded health care workers to the Government of Malawi. The use of the government's payroll systems generates commitment and accountability in support of locally led development..This activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.2 - Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance and 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and are able to contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work.

title.narrative: Mangochi District Council - Health and HIV Treatment Activity (Government -to - Government)

description.narrative: (Malawi): In line with USAID's vision of system strengthening for greater sustainability and resilience, USAID entered into a direct three-year government to government agreement with Mangochi District Council. This integrated health activity will implement critical health activities that will contribute to the improvement of maternal and child health; voluntary family planning; and nutrition service delivery. FY 2022 funds will enable the Mangochi District Council to: 1) implement family health services through integrated outreach and mobile visits; 2) strengthen the procurement of essential equipment, data collection, and usage; 3) operationalize the community health strategy; and 4) provide supportive supervision and on-the-job mentoring to promote quality of care at facility and community levels. The activity will support the recruitment of two hundred and thirty one priority health care workers and one support staff using the Government of Malawi's recruitment and salary payment systems. The direct funding support will enhance Malawi's pathway to locally led development through building sustainable and resilient health systems with increased efficiency, transparency, and accountability..This activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.2 - Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance and 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work...

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Community Partnerships for Sustainable Resource Management in Malawi (COMPASS II)

description.narrative: The purpose of COMPASS II is to enhance household revenue from participation in CBNRM initiatives that generate income as well as provide incentives for sustainable resource use in Malawi. Building on the solid foundation established under NATURE, MAFE, and COMPASS towards building capacity of the Malawian government and nongovernmental organizations to adopt strategies that ensure long-term economic and environmental sustainability, COMPASS II seeks to accomplish three objectives: 1. Increase the decentralization of natural resource management, 2. Enhance rural communities' capacity to sustainably manage their natural resources, and 3. Increase sales of natural resources-based products.

Launched in October 2021, BFG is a three-year initiative to address mobility challenges in rural and periurban areas in sub-Saharan Africa by developing and demonstrating the means to promote functional bicycle market systems leading to rapid increases in bicycle access and uptake. BFG has two phases. In the first phase, BFG is conducting market systems assessments of the supply, demand, and supporting systems for bicycles in Ghana, Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda, and Zambia, leading to reports such as this one. Based on the results of the assessment phase, BFG will implement pilot projects in four to six localities across two of the targeted countries. The pilots will reduce barriers to the supply and uptake of fit-for-purpose, affordable, and durable bicycles. In addition to the assessments and pilots, BFG is identifying local partners in each country to serve as Convening Partners and members of Bicycle Market System Advisory Committees, which will continue to advocate and serve the interests of bicycle market stakeholders, building on the work of the assessments.

description.narrative: Testing a budgeting intervention to address seasonal hunger. With support from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), researchers at the Center for Effective Global Action (CEGA) conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with over 800 subsistence farmers in 113 villages in Zambias Eastern province to evaluate a low-cost behavioral intervention designed to help smallholder farmers use a structured planning process to allocate their annual income to last until the next harvest. The intervention, carried out shortly after the annual maize harvest, consists of training farmers to use simple planning boards divided into various income and expense categories, helping participants to generate realistic spending estimates and budget their harvest income to smooth consumption throughout the year. Farmers keep the planning boards to remind them of their plans and receive physical labels for their bags of maize that reflect their spending plan for the upcoming year. The evaluation found that the intervention increased savings for the families who had been randomly assigned to receive the intervention. As discussed in the policy brief, four months after the intervention, these households entered the hunger season with 20 percent more savings (approximately an additional months worth of savings) than their control group counterparts. These extra savings meant that farmers were 32 percent less likely to take second jobs to meet their subsistence needs and therefore could dedicate more time and savings to strategic investments in their farms, which resulted in 9 percent higher crop revenues during the following years harvest. These results affirm that a simple 45-minute budget forecasting exercise can help farmers stretch savings longer into the hunger season and ultimately increase their farm investment and harvest the following year.

title.narrative: Testing Phone-Based Targeting for Urban Social Protection

description.narrative: Low-income countries spend an average of 1.5 percent of GDP on social protection programs, but significant gaps in coverage result in only 18 percent of the poorest households receiving the program benefits for which they are eligible. GiveDirectly aims to address the inefficiency and high cost of identifying and enrolling recipients with MobileAid, its eligibility assessment model that leverages machine learning and cell phone data to identify the extreme poor and then deliver benefits via mobile money transfers. With funding from DIV, GiveDirectly, in partnership with researchers from the University of Berkeley and the Government of Malawi, will evaluate the comparative accuracy and cost-effectiveness of different targeting methods for identifying households eligible for cash transfers. GiveDirectlys approach could significantly improve the speed, efficiency, and accuracy of urban poverty targeting in Malawi and serve as a model for other countries.

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID is strengthening Malawi's democratic culture and improving trust in electoral institutions through the Malawi Electoral Integrity Program (MEIP). MEIP supports electoral institutions and civil society partners to: strengthen election management; increase access to information; enhance issue-based engagement with democratic institutions; and build the capacity of elected leaders of parliament..MEIP's assistance was critical in restoring integrity and public confidence in Malawi's electoral systems following the court-annulled 2019 Presidential election. The successful 2020 Presidential election, evidenced by strong leadership within the Malawi Electoral Commission, Parliament, and a robust civil society, offers promising opportunities to institutionalize reforms and further increase the transparency and accountability of electoral stakeholders. Using FY 2020 funds, MEIP will: 1) expand its support for electoral reforms and improved electoral administration; 2) enhance civil society knowledge around elections, with particular attention to emerging priorities in the post-2020 presidential elections environment; 3) support parliamentary committees to effectively perform their oversight and legislative functions; 4) support the parliamentary youth caucus to debate on youth issues; and, 5) enhance U.S. government diplomacy in the post-election period by leveraging MEIP's support to parliament and electoral institutions. ..Strengthening political processes is a priority under Objectives 2.2 of the Joint Strategic Plan and the National Security Strategy's political priority actions that include working with promising nations to develop institutions accountable and responsive to citizens. MEIP further contributes to the Malawi Integrated Country Strategy's Goal 2: promote a more responsive, transparent, and accountable government as well as Objective 2.2: citizens exercise rights and responsibilities. .

title.narrative: Modern Cooking for Healthy Forests in Malawi - Tiphike Mwa Makono

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Modern Cooking for Healthy Forests (MCHF) activity promotes sustainable forest management in select landscapes and alternative clean energy options for cooking in targeted urban areas to reduce illegal charcoal use, which is the main driver of deforestation.MCHF will utilize FY2022 Climate Change-Adaptation funds to strengthen diversified livelihoods; increase incomes and assets of vulnerable communities and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs); reduce communities' vulnerability to climate change impacts; leverage economic opportunities; and improve natural resource management. Specifically, MCHF will build the capacity of over 30 early-stage entrepreneurs and other established companies promoting clean cooking solutions and forest-/restoration-friendly enterprises to reduce an over-dependence on charcoal use and help restore degraded lands. By growing MSMEs and supporting entrepreneurs, MCHF helps Malawians move away from more climate-sensitive livelihoods. MCHF will also continue to support forest governance at local levels, working with stakeholders to develop forest management plans; collect and use data; build the capacity of village natural resources management, including their understanding and awareness of issues of tenure, access rights, and benefit sharing; conflict resolution; and forest fire prevention and management. USAID will support community groups to scale-up land restoration in degraded hot spots to create healthy ecosystems, diversify livelihoods, and reduce climate risk thereby increasing community and ecosystem resilience to climate variability.This activity supports the Mission's Integrated Country Strategy Objective 2.3 - Nurture entrepreneurship, unleashing the ingenuity of the Malawian people to self-realize a better economic future. .

title.narrative: Optimizing HIV Services for Epidemic Control (OHSEC)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Optimizing HIV/AIDS Services for Epidemic Control activity in Malawi supports the National Tuberculosis (TB) Program to implement the National TB Strategy nationwide. FY 2019 funds will enable the activity to: 1) strengthen the TB laboratory and diagnostic network by building the capacity of national and district level staff; 2) maintain a Service Level Agreement and warranty with the service provider of Gxalert real-time connectivity which ensures real-time reporting of various TB testing services to a centralized database; 3) enroll new Xpert machines added to the network on the Service Level Agreement and warranty; 4) support the implementation of Xpert scale-up and Universal Drug Sensitivity Testing as the new standard of care; 5) ensure linkage to treatment of diagnosed drug-resistant TB patients; 6) support the National TB Program to respond rapidly to issues reported through Gxalert, including follow-up of diagnosed drug resistant patients, forecasting and redistributing test cartridges, determine and organize additional training and support; and 7) build the capacity of the National TB reference and district laboratories. As a local organization with significant technical capacity and experience on USAID and the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief programming, Partners in Hope is well-positioned and experienced to lead the TB control efforts in Malawi. The interventions implemented by this activity support the Integrated Country Strategy and are in line with the existing U.S. government Global TB Strategy with a vision to reach every person with TB, cure those in need of treatment, and prevent disease progression and new infections and the USAID Global Accelerator to End TB, USAID's contribution to the United Nation's target of treating 40 million people between 2018 and 2022. .

title.narrative: Restoring Fisheries for Sustainable Livelihoods in Lake Malawi (REFRESH)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's REFRESH activity addresses priority threats to biodiversity while diversifying livelihoods to reduce climate risk for healthy ecosystems and increased climate resilience for Malawians e involved in the fisheries industry. Covering all eight of the districts bordering Lake Malawi, REFRESH in its second year of implementation will: (1) build capacity among communities and districts to form and/or strengthen local fisheries management authorities to develop and implement local fisheries plans, link to district councils, increase revenue, and support enforcement; (2) support the National Fisheries Research Unit to conduct total catch and fishing intensity assessments, which support commercial and artisanal fisheries with scientifically sound management regimes; (3) train the Fisheries Enforcement Unit to combat and successfully prosecute illegal, unregulated, and unreported fishing crimes in Lake Malawi; (4) scale up conservation enterprises to help reduce pressure on wild caught fisheries; and, (5) build constituencies for effective, accountable, and transparent ecosystem-based fisheries management. .By 2024, REFRESH will result in: (1) the establishment of 1,500,000 hectares of biologically significant area for improved natural resource management that include fish sanctuaries and estuaries identified in the International Union for Conservation of Nature's Key Biodiversity Areas for Lake Malawi. In addition, REFRESH will result in a stronger and more sustainable fisheries sector - the country's main source of protein and critical for nutrition; build citizen capacity at district level, with strengthened Beach Village Committees and District Councils; support conservation enterprises; and establish sustainable financing mechanisms. .This activity will support the Mission's ICS Objective 2.3 - Nurture entrepreneurship, unleashing the ingenuity of the Malawian people to self-realize a better economic future..

The goal of REFAM is to develop a scalable intervention that allows for the screening, identification, placement, instruction, and testing of learners with disabilities in order to teach them to read.

title.narrative: Expanding Malawi HIV/AIDS Prevention with Local Organizations Working for an Effective Epidemic Response (EMPOWER)

description.narrative: EMPOWER is a five-year program, funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development, with the goal of preventing new HIV infections in targeted populations in priority districts in Malawi. Jhpiego is leading a consortium to implement EMPOWERs voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) component in Chikwawa, Thyolo and Zomba. Building on Jhpiegos previous experience supporting VMMC services in these districts, the consortium is collaborating with stakeholders to increase uptake of high-quality VMMC services among males aged 1529 in these districts, with a goal of achieving 80% coverage and linking those testing HIV-positive to care and treatment. To reach this goal, the consortium is: 1) increasing availability of and access to VMMC services; 2) increasing demand for VMMC among the targeted age groups; 3) improving the quality of VMMC services; and 4) strengthening linkages between VMMC and other services.

title.narrative: Expanding Malawi HIV/AIDS Prevention with local Organizations Working for an Effective Epidemic Response (EMPOWER) - Determined, Resilient, Empowered, AIDS-free, Mentored, and Safe (DREAMS)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's PEPFAR-funded activity - Expanding Malawi HIV/AIDS Prevention with local Organizations Working for an Effective Epidemic Response (EMPOWER) - will provide youth-friendly health services to adolescent girls and young women aged 10 - 24 years enrolled in the Determined, Resilient, Empowered, AIDS-free, Mentored, and Safe (DREAMS) program to prevent the acquisition and transmission of HIV and expand access to reproductive healthcare. FY 2020 Family Planning funds will leverage PEPFAR investments to provide comprehensive, integrated services, including voluntary family planning, emergency contraception, HIV prevention, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), post-exposure prophylaxis, and gender-based/intimate partner violence (screening and response) services. EMPOWER will roll-out PrEP by systematically including eligibility screening, provision, and adherence support as part of the integrated package at community-based, youth-friendly points of service. EMPOWER will enroll adolescent girls and young women in DREAMS clubs in their communities to ensure that they access the services they need. This activity is part of the overall preventing child, early, and forced (CEFM) marriage activity in Machinga. .This activity aligns with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.1 - Improve socio-economic development...

Grant men access to comprehensive, safe, high-quality, and cost-effective VMMC services, promote condoms as part of a comprehensive approach to HIV/AIDS programming across PEPFAR projects and management of the DREAMS database.

title.narrative: National Reading Program Implementation and Expansion (NRPIE) Activity

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's National Reading Program Implementation and Expansion (NRPIE) activity provides technical assistance via a U.S. university partnership to the Ministry of Education's (MOE) Department of Quality Assurance and the Malawi Institute of Education. FY 2021 funds will be used to continue providing technical support from Florida State University (FSU) to the Malawi Institute of Education to: 1) develop upper primary level Chichewa and English teaching and learning materials, and 2) to align these materials to a revised Scope and Sequence. The activity will facilitate the transfer of technical skills from FSU to the Malawi Institute of Education to manage and sustain a comprehensive instructional material development system in line with its mandate to support the implementation of Malawi's national curriculum. .This activity supports the ICS Mission Objective 3.3 - Malawi expands educational opportunity to equip its citizens with foundational and marketable skills responsive to Malawi's public and private sector needs. The activity supports the Mission's strategy through endeavouring to strengthen capacities of a public sector institution through the transfer of skills and knowledge from U.S. higher education institutions to improve the quality of materials for use in service delivery..

title.narrative: Leveraging Local Capacity to Strengthen Health Service Delivery Project (LLCAP) - Human Resources for Health (HRH1)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Leveraging Local Capacity to Strengthen Health Service Delivery Project-Human Resources for Health (HRH#1) is an integrated health activity designed to improve the number and availability of well-trained, highly-skilled, and equitably distributed healthcare workers. The activity will support the delivery of quality health services in line with the National Health Sector Strategic Plan and will advance the Government of Malawi's universal health coverage to improve the health status of Malawians...Implemented by the Global Aids Interfaith Alliance (GAIA), the activity will: 1) increase the number and availability of trained personnel and qualified health workers in priority health areas; 2) improve the quality of health services through enhancing staff capacity in pre-service and in-service education; and 3) strengthen the capacity of the Government of Malawi to effectively monitor and regulate health care service providers in the country, including data collection, analysis, and interpretation for evidence based decisions. To achieve the stated objectives, the activity will provide pre-service scholarships for nurses and midwives; recruit and provide salaries for newly graduated nurses and midwives; and provide clinical mentors for training institutions and hospitals. GAIA will support higher institutions to develop curriculum to train healthcare workers to respond to health needs during and after climate related emergencies. GAIA is a local organization and through this mechanism USAID enhances local institutional capacity that will ensure program continuity after the activity closes out...The activity enhances Malawi's pathway to locally led development and aligns with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work......

title.narrative: Leveraging Local Capacity to Strengthen Health Service Delivery Project (LLCAP) - Human Resources for Health (HRH2)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Leveraging Local Capacity to Strengthen Health Service Delivery Project-Human Resources for Health (HRH#2) is an integrated activity designed to provide scholarships to improve the availability of well-trained, highly-skilled, and equitably distributed healthcare workforce. The activity will support the delivery of quality health services and will advance the Government of Malawi's National Health Sector Strategic Plan for universal health coverage...Implemented by the Malawi College of Health Sciences (MCHS), the activity will: 1) increase the number and availability of trained and qualified frontline health workers in priority health areas, 2) improve the quality of pre-service education, and 3) increase access to educational opportunities for health workers. To achieve the stated objectives, the activity will specifically train nurse midwife technicians; community midwife assistants; pharmacy assistants; nurses and midwives; assistant environmental health officers; and medical assistants. Additionally, the activity will improve the quality of pre-service education using a training model that equips students with preventive, clinical, nursing, and management of health services. The activity also will support higher education entities to develop a curriculum that promotes a multisectoral approach to respond to health needs during and after climate related emergencies. MCHS is a local organization owned and run by the Government of Malawi. Through this activity, USAID enhances local institutional capacity that will ensure program continuity after the activity closes out. ..The activity enhances Malawi's pathway to locally led development and aligns with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work..

title.narrative: Leveraging Local Capacity to Strengthen Health Service Delivery - Human Resource for Health (HRH #3) - Nutrition

description.narrative: (Malawi): Leveraging Local Capacity to Strengthen Health Service Delivery-Human Resource for Health (HRH#3) - Nutrition 4 Health activity will strengthen the Government of Malawi's capacity to accelerate long-term and sustained responses to address high burden nutritional disorders such as stunting, wasting, underweight, and micronutrient deficiencies. As such, this activity will strengthen Malawi's capacity to effectively respond to nutrition and social problems affecting the health of Malawians, thereby accelerating the overall economic development. ..To achieve its objectives, the activity will: i) train and deploy a critical mass of dietitians for all referral and district hospitals in Malawi; ii) establish an association of dietitians in Malawi to govern the dietetic profession and practice; iii) update the food composition database and tables containing no less than six hundred foods that are commonly consumed in Malawi; iv) strengthen research, outreach, and teaching capacity in nutrition, dietetics, and food science at Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Sciences; v) train staff at Masters and PhD levels in Nutrition and Dietetics, and undertake and publish ethically-sound research; vi) develop a curriculum in nutrition that will respond to health needs during and after climate related emergencies. USAID's support to Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Sciences enhances local institutional capacity to ensure program continuity after the activity closes out. ..The activity supports the State-USAID Joint Regional Strategy Goal 4.3 to sustainably reduce hunger, malnutrition, and poverty in sub-Saharan Africa. The activity also supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.2 Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work....

title.narrative: Tigwirane Manja Counter - Trafficking in Persons Activity

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Tigwirane Manja (translated as: lets join hands to fight human trafficking) Counter-Trafficking in Persons (C-TIP) activity will work to combat human trafficking in Malawi. Trafficking in Persons impacts on the rights of victims and their potential for full human development. This activity will focus on four key areas, namely prevention of trafficking in persons; improving the number of prosecutions of trafficking offenders; improving protection of survivors and management of shelters; and finally it will work to improve data collection and usage. The areas mentioned are part of the recommendations made in the 2020 State Department report for Malawi. By implementing these recommendations, the Government of Malawi and its partners will be able to deal with human trafficking issue..The Tigwirane Manja C-TIP activity will work with the National Coordinating Committee Against Trafficking in Person, a high-level ministerial committee headed by the Ministry of Homeland Security, and its civil society partners under the Malawi Network Against Human Trafficking. .The Tigwirane Manja C-TIP activity contributes to the Malawi ICS's Goal 3: Human Capital Development; and Objective 3.1 - Malawi improves individual and community agency to an extent that its citizens become more productive, engaged, and resilient. The activity also contributes to CDCS 2020-2025 DO 1/Intermediate Result 1.1 - citizens' rights and responsibility actively exercised; DO 2/Intermediate Result 2.1 - youth agency and access to opportunities and services expanded; and, DO 3/Intermediate Result 3.1 - resilient people, households, communities, and systems manage and reduce vulnerabilities.

(Malawi): The Upper Primary Reading (UPRead) activity will improve the reading and writing skills of Standards 5-8 learners by developing quality and relevant Chichewa and English instructional and supplementary reading materials. UPRead will prepare learners to "read to learn", excel in Primary School Leaving Certificate of Education examinations, and to be literate for life. The activity will strengthen the institutional capacity of the Malawi Institute of Education to manage and sustain a comprehensive instructional materials development system under Malawi's NRP. UPRead will support Malawi Institute of Education in the areas of: technical capacity for the curriculum development and design process, operational capacity for sustainability, and development of quality and relevant instructional and supplementary materials for upper primary English and Chichewa..UPRead will develop the following materials: Standards 5-8 English and Chichewa scope and sequence, learners' books, teachers' guides, supplementary readers, a supplementary resource guide, a continuous assessment and remediation manual, and syllabi. These materials will have an extensive reach, covering all the 34 education districts in Malawi and targeting 5,641 public primary schools, benefitting over 32,000 teachers and 1,819,596 Standards 5 to 8 learners. .UPRead supports the U.S. government's Basic Education Strategy, underscoring the importance of equal access to relevant, quality education; and the ICS Mission Objective 3.3 - Malawi expands educational opportunity to equip its citizens with foundational and marketable skills responsive to Malawi's public and private sector needs. UPRead supports the Mission's Strategy through endeavouring to strengthen capacities of the Malawi Institute of Education to develop high quality curricular materials sustainably..

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Tuberculosis Local Organization Network-1 (TB LON-1) activity in Malawi will support the National Tuberculosis and Leprosy Elimination Program to implement the TB National Strategic plan. TB-LON-1 will use FY 2022 funds to support: 1) implementation of a more effective shortened, fully-oral treatment regimen for drug-resistant TB (DR-TB); 2) secondment of three laboratory technologists at the national and regional TB culture labs; 3) scaling-up of new World Health Organization recommended TB molecular testing tools including GeneXpert and TrueNat which will improve access to bacterial and TB drug sensitivity testing; 4) scaling-up of the use of stool-based specimen in pediatric TB screening on Xpert or similar machine; 5) linking of diagnosed TB patients including drug-resistant TB patients to treatment; 6) implementation of TB testing quality improvement/quality assurance strategies; 7) TB screening among prison inmates; 8) leveraging of PEPFAR funding to support TB/HIV services; and 9) maintenance of a service contract for GxAlert/Aspect software; a remote cloud-based data monitoring system and automatic electronic system for Xpert diagnostic devices with real-time TB results reporting including drug resistance for timely patients care initiation. .TB LON-1 is aligned with the U.S. government's Global TB Strategy and the USAID's Global Accelerator business model to End TB that support the goal of reaching every person with TB, curing those in need of treatment, and preventing disease progression and new infections. TB LON-1 supports the Joint Strategic Plan Objective 1.1: Strengthen global health security, combat infectious disease threats, and address priority global health challenges through bilateral engagement and within multilateral fora....

(Malawi): USAID's Tuberculosis Local Organizations Network-2 (TB LON-2) activity will support the National Tuberculosis and Leprosy Elimination Program to implement its strategic plan by addressing TB programmatic gaps with locally generated solutions. TB LON-2 will use FY 2022 funds to: 1) implement an active TB case finding intervention at twenty one health facilities in three high-burden districts and link the diagnosed TB patients to effective treatment; 2) implement the TB treatment guideline on shortened, fully-oral treatment regimen for drug resistant TB; 3) improve access to timely and quality diagnosis, effective prevention, treatment, and care services for TB while reducing stigma, creating demand, and addressing patient and community TB treatment needs; 4) implement innovative strategies for contact investigation of pulmonary TB patients; 5) scale-up the use of stool-based specimen to detect TB in children; and 6) build the capacity of health facility staff and community volunteers including those from private not-for-profit facilities in TB screening, prevention, and treatment. ..TB LON-2 is aligned with the U.S. government's Global TB Strategy and the USAID's Global Accelerator business model to End TB that support the goal of reaching every person with TB, curing those in need of treatment, and preventing disease progression and new infections. TB LON-2 supports the Joint Strategic Plan Objective 1.1: Strengthen global health security, combat infectious disease threats, and address priority global health challenges through bilateral engagement and within multilateral fora. The activity also supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.2: Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and are able to contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work.....

title.narrative: Let Them Grow Healthy (Akule ndi Thanzi)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Let Them Grow Healthy activity will work with private sector partners and serve as the primary community-based platform for the delivery of a wide range of water, sanitation, and hygiene; nutrition, and maternal and child health interventions. With FY22 funds, the activity will finance community-level efforts to consult with mothers and caregivers on care and feeding practices for infants and young children. Using the Care Group Model, the activity will: 1) conduct nutrition education to improve knowledge and practices; 2) strengthen community referral and support systems for pregnant women and children under-5; 3) promote adequate women's nutrition, exclusive breastfeeding, and complementary feeding through social behavior change; 4) construct boreholes and rehabilitate non-functional ones; 5) facilitate the creation of open defecation-free communities; 6) promote access and adoption of improved water and sanitation services, and hygiene practices. .The activity also promotes complementary interventions such as soy processing, fruit-tree propagation, and cultivation of orange-fleshed sweet potatoes. This approach will bolster community members' confidence, capacity, and skills to act as agents of their own development process. The activity will improve the health and nutrition status of under-5 children in targeted districts. These interventions will improve nutrition and overall health outcomes among vulnerable children and women by providing cleaner and reliable water supply, diet diversity, and associated social and behavior change programming..The activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission 3.1-Malawi improves individual and community agency to an extent that its citizens become more productive, engaged, and resilient, and 3.2-Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work.....

title.narrative: Strengthening Parliament’s Role in Malawi’s Development (SPRID)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Strengthening Parliament's Role in Malawi's Development activity contributes to Malawi's democratic governance by supporting Parliament of Malawi to better fulfill its legislative, oversight, and representative functions. The activity bolsters the effectiveness and independence of Parliament by providing technical support to selected constitutional and standing committees. The activity will provide embedded experts in parliamentary research to help develop a specialized and adequately staffed committee system, able to work through parliament's legislative and oversight functions, to address key public integrity and service delivery. To restore public trust, the activity will provide technical assistance to enhance coordination between parliament and statutory oversight bodies such as the anti-corruption bureau, so they can take timely preventive and corrective action on public accountability issues. The activity will provide technical support to civil society organizations and the media, to help them best utilize the access to information law and build a constructive relationship with Parliament that advances the public interest. By engaging Parliament, civil society and media can ensure that Parliament is responsive and accountable to the public. Parliament in turn can work through civil society and media to leverage public support for their legislative and oversight priorities. The activity aligns with the ICS's Goal 1: Democratic and Accountable Governance; and Objective 1.1 Support Malawian institutions, including parliament, the judiciary, and accountability institutions, to make governance more effective, transparent, and accountable. It also supports USAID/Malawi's 2020 - 2025 Country Development Cooperation Strategy (CDCS) Development Objective 1, which seeks to improve public sector effectiveness and accountability at the national and decentralized levels.

title.narrative: Moving Integrated, Quality Maternal, Newborn, Child Health and Family Planning and Reproductive Health Services to Scale (MOMENTUM/Tiyeni) Activity Component 1

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Moving Integrated, Quality Maternal, Newborn, Child Health and Family Planning and Reproductive Health (MNCH/FP/RH) Services to Scale (MOMENTUM/Tiyeni) activity will support the Government of Malawi's effort to reduce maternal, newborn, and child morbidity and mortality through improved access and quality of health service delivery in seven districts. It will focus on MNCH; voluntary FP/RH; nutrition; water, sanitation, and hygiene; and malaria prevention and treatment. It will deploy integrated and age-appropriate interventions through facility and community-based approaches. With FY 2022 funds, MOMENTUM/Tiyeni will: 1) provide mentorship, coaching, and supervision of health workers in targeted districts, 2) contribute towards ending child, early, and forced marriages, 3) support health governance and accountability using data for decision-making, quality improvement activities, and civil society organizations engagement, 4) provide targeted market-based technical assistance to expand the private sector's role in health service delivery, and provide technical assistance to Government-to-Government supported districts, 5) support social and behavior change interventions to improve health-seeking behaviors, and maximize access to life-saving commodities and high-quality health services, and 6) improve communication between health providers and clients, families, and couples. The activity will support contingency plans to respond to health needs during and after climate related emergencies, The activity will also use timely surveillance data to forecast health outcomes and adjust program objectives to optimize results through adaptive management to mitigate outbreaks..The activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work..

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Governance for Solutions works through local coalitions of stakeholders in government, private sector, and civil society to identify governance bottlenecks that inhibit effective delivery of public services, efficient use of public resources, and the protection of public goods such as natural resources. The activity will help identify groups or institutions that are effectively addressing these challenges; learn from these experiences; devise interventions that build on success; and adapt programming for further improvement. GfS will identify issues based on the USAID/Malawi's CDCS and the viability of coalitions in effecting change. Health, education, agriculture, and natural resources management are key GfS sectors, with human resource and financial management as cross-cutting challenges. Illustrative issues include teacher performance, drug theft, and more efficient agricultural subsidies that have direct and attributable impacts on aid effectiveness and the Mission's development objectives..GfS contributes to the Malawi ICS's Goal 1: Democratic and Accountable Governance; and Objective 1.2 Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance. It also supports CDCS (2020 - 2025) Development Objective 1, which seeks to improve public sector effectiveness and accountability at the national and decentralized levels. The activity also prioritizes the cross-cutting goals of gender equity and youth engagement....

title.narrative: Next Generation Early Grade Reading (NextGen) Flagship Activity

description.narrative: (Malawi): Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will complete a performance evaluation of the Next Generation Early Grade Reading flagship activity (NextGen). Building on the U.S. government's investments in the National Reading Program, the evaluation will support the Ministry of Education and continue to build its capacity in conducting National Reading Assessments to measure students' reading outcomes. The evaluation will also inform the learning and adaptive management of NextGen and its contributions to USAID-supported National Reading Program objectives. The evaluation will meet the requirements for evaluating large activities set forth in ADS 201 and will enhance evidence-based decision making related to early grade and pre-primary reading interventions, It will support the U.S. government's Basic Education Strategy and the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.3 - Malawi expands educational opportunity to equip its citizens with foundational and marketable skills responsive to Malawi's public and private sector needs. This evaluation will also support the Mission's strategy development objective: "Youth lead healthy, informed, and productive lives". ..

(Malawi): USAID's Transforming Higher Education Systems activity in Malawi will foster productive partnerships between U.S. and Malawi higher education institutions (HEIs) to address issues of educational access, equity, relevance, and quality. Transforming Higher Education Systems activity will prioritize strengthening Malawian universities' capacities to increase market-linked program offerings, research and innovation in areas relevant to the country's economic growth with specific attention to agriculture and value addition. With FY 2022 funds, Transforming Higher Education Systems activity will work to: strengthen the human and institutional capacities of Malawian HEIs to design and deliver high quality, diversified, and market-relevant degrees and short courses; expand access to these high quality higher education courses, particularly for adolescent girls and young women, people with disabilities, students graduating from community day secondary schools especially in rural areas, and other disadvantaged youth; improve research and innovation outputs from Malawian HEIs; improve collaboration between Malawian HEIs and industry; improve governance systems of the Malawian higher education sub-sector, including governance of Malawian HEIs; and strengthen or establish student protection systems at Malawian HEIs.This activity will increase access to quality education and support the Integrated Country Strategy Goal 3: human capital development, specifically under Mission Objective 3.3 - Malawi expands educational opportunities to equip its citizens with foundational and marketable skills responsive to Malawi's public and private sector needs. It also furthers the goals of the USAID's 2020-2025 CDCS which seeks to support Malawi to become more self-reliant, gender equitable, and democratically accountable..

Local Works Experimental Activity that seeks to improve the land rights of peri-urban land holders for the realization of social, political and economic rights by conducting a research and testing interventions that will potentially improve land administration and management, and land titling processes and, increase access to information on land administration and management for citizens.

title.narrative: CONCERT (Communicating, Networking, and Capacity-Building To Effectively Respond Together)

description.narrative: CONCERT aims to reduce fertility and population growth; lower the risk of HIV/AIDS; and reduce maternal and infant and under-five mortality rates. The project has broad national coverage through mass media, campaigns, and capacity building, as well as intensive implementation through projects local partners. During the life of the project, CONCERT will: 1) Work to improve coordination and planning by developing a platform for health messaging and integrated communication strategies. 2) Develop a multi-media campaign using a centrepiece radio programme and family health booklet. 3) Develop a community mobilization toolkit. 4) Support capacity development of the HEU and explore the creation of an S/BCC knowledge management system. 5) Develop and document best practices, introducing new approaches to S/BCC and conduct operations research.

description.narrative: (Malawi): .USAID/Malawi's Adventist Health Services (AHS) activity will increase the provision and knowledge of family planning (FP) services for youth, women, and men of reproductive age in Blantyre, Dedza, Mzimba, and Rumphi districts of Malawi. AHS will use the Community Action Group methodology to engage communities, with a focus on male involvement, to increase knowledge and acceptability of FP services. Activities will include: (a) train additional health care workers on FP service delivery, especially community-based distribution agents (CBDAs) and health surveillance assistants; (b) promote community-based distribution of short-term FP methods; (c) use mobile outreach clinics to increase access to Long-acting and Permanent Methods of FP in hard to reach areas of Blantyre; (d) conduct community sensitization on the benefits of FP; and (e) train men as CBDAs. These activities will result in increased demand, access, and use of FP on the part of community members..

title.narrative: Strengthening Early Grade Reading in Malawi (SEGREM)

description.narrative: (Malawi): The Malawi education system has very low learning outcomes on national reading assessments for primary students. Low quality curriculum materials are a key contributing factor. The SEGREM activity supports the Ministry of Education, Science, and Technology in the implementation of the National Reading Program through the production of relevant, quality teaching and learning materials. The activity developed the language and literacy instructional materials for Standards 1 to 4 Chichewa and English, including teacher guides, student textbooks, syllabi, and supplementary readers that will reach 3,409,817 standard 1-4 learners enrolled across the 5,603 primary schools in Malawi. SEGREM will refine and expand English and Chichewa teaching and learning materials for Standards 1-4, such as curriculum pacing guides, age-appropriate supplementary student reading materials, and open-source and student books for private market sale. These tasks address two of the deficiencies attributed to children's failure to read in Malawi: inappropriate pedagogy and outdated materials. .Implemented by the Malawi Institute of Education, a Government of Malawi (GoM) parastatal, it is the only entity responsible for curriculum development for Malawian primary and secondary schools and Teacher's Training Colleges. SEGREM staff are qualified curriculum development specialists with the skills to develop curriculum materials, and, benefit from USAID's technical assistance. The SEGREM activity increases access to quality reading materials in schools and at home which in turn will improve students' reading ability and learning outcomes. It works through existing government structures, hence supporting the U.S. Foreign Policy priority of ensuring self-reliance and the U.S. Government Basic Education Strategy....

Objectives for Malawi: Implemented by the Malawi Institute of Education, a parastatal organization, SEGREM reviews, revises, and creates reading materials and textbooks for the National Reading Program. It is also implementing an activity to improve primary teachers’ mastery of the English language.

title.narrative: The Girls’ Empowerment through Education and Health (ASPIRE) Activity

description.narrative: (Malawi): .USAID/Malawi's ASPIRE: Girl's Empowerment through Education and Health Activity improves reading skills for girls aged 10-19 in upper primary school, for a strong foundation to help them succeed in secondary school. It incorporates PEPFAR, WASH, and Basic Education funding. FY 2016 Activities include: Performing targeted assessments, including an English proficiency assessment for teachers; Training teachers to improve students' advanced reading skills; Coaching primary teachers to implement the new strategies; Providing materials for students to practice their skills; and engaging communities and students in activities that promote a reading culture. Activities will result in improved learning outcomes for girls; enhanced adoption of child-friendly school models; raised awareness of HIV/AIDs and sexual reproductive health rights; increased awareness of WASH issues; and increased community support for girls' education and health in Malawi....

Objectives for Malawi: ASPIRE is designed to specifically address the challenges that girls face in the Malawian Education system. It is a collaborative, co-funded activity between USAID/Malawi’s Education and Health Offices and implemented by Save the Children Federation Inc. that focuses on all primary and secondary schools in the Balaka, Machinga, and Zomba districts. The main goals are to improve the reading skills of girls in upper primary school, increase the adoption of positive sexual and health-care seeking behaviors, and decrease key structural and cultural barriers to girls’ access to schooling.
One Community

(Malawi): .The Pamawa ndi a Chinyamata activity will invest $400,000 of FY 2016 adaptation resources and $200,000 of FY 2016 family planning and reproductive health resources to increase the adoption of positive behaviors related to climate change adaptation (CCA), sexual reproductive health (SRH), and family planning (FP) among youth in Balaka, Machinga and Mangochi Districts..The activity will: ..develop a social behavioral change communication strategy on integrated CCA and SRH/FP messages and communication channels for the youth; ..mobilize 200 youth clubs into radio listening clubs to raise awareness of the link between increased population and communities' vulnerability to climate change; and ..conduct a qualitative study on the link between climate change resilience and population dynamics...Activities will result in communities' increased capacity for undertaking practical local adaptive strategies and increased access to reproductive health and FP information and services....

(Malawi): USAID's Tiwalere II activity in Malawi is a private sector engagement initiative between USAID and Feed the Children and its corporate partners, Nu Skin and Procter and Gamble. Tiwalere II delivers high-impact interventions targeting children under the age of five and women, with a special focus on the 1,000 days between conception and age two. Using FY 2019 funds, the activity will finance community-level workers' efforts to consult with mothers and caregivers on the care and feeding practices of infants and young children. Tiwalere II will conduct nutrition education to improve knowledge and practices; strengthen community referral and support systems for pregnant women and children under the age of five; promote adequate women's nutrition, exclusive breastfeeding, and complementary feeding through social behavior change; construct boreholes and maintain non- functional ones; facilitate the creation of open defecation-free communities and promote access to improved water and sanitation services and the adoption of improved hygiene practices; and promote bed net usage to prevent malaria. The activity also has interventions in irrigation farming, winter cropping, fruit tree propagation, and orange-fleshed sweet potato cultivation. The Care Group Model approach that Tiwalere provides at the community level serves as a powerful social and behavioral change tool. The approach reinforces community members' confidence and the capacity and skills to act as agents of their own development process, and it fosters self-reliance. The activity will improve the health and nutrition status of under-five children in targeted districts in central and northern Malawi and is fundamental to achieving Joint Regional Strategy Goal 4.3?sustainably reducing hunger, malnutrition and poverty in sub-Saharan Africa. Good nutrition is essential for reducing maternal and child mortality around the world and reaching the Preventing Child and Maternal Deaths goals. ...

title.narrative: Early Grade Reading Activity (EGRA) Impact Evaluation (IE)

description.narrative: (Malawi): .USAID/Malawi's Early Grade Reading Activity Impact Evaluation (EGRAIE) has two distinct objectives. One is to assess the impact and the effectiveness of the Early Grade Reading Activity (EGRA) and the other is to perform National Reading Assessments to assess the level at which all standard 2 and 4 students are reading against the nationally set reading benchmarks. The EGRAIE will collect, analyze, and report the endline data on EGRA interventions and control schools to provide an impact analysis of EGRA reading interventions on the reading skills of students in standards 2 and 4. Activity results will validate the effect of EGRA on students' reading abilities in communities where USAID is providing education, health, environment, and agriculture interventions (called "full integration districts") as well as in other EGRA districts ("partial: or "non" integration districts) where USAID/Malawi is not implementing its full package of activities..

Objectives for Malawi: This activity, implemented by School to School International, provides expert technical assistance to the MoEST to develop a comprehensive implementation plan for the National Reading Program. This program incorporates the four main components of the National Reading Strategy: instruction, assessment, teacher preparation, and family and community participation.

(Malawi): USAID/Malawi's Early Grade Reading Activity (EGRA) works with the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology to improve the reading skills of students in Standards 1-3. Reading achievement, documented through several assessments, consistently shows Malawi ranking at the bottom in the Southern African Development Community region for primary student reading skills. FY 2015 activities include:-In-service training for teachers, head teachers, and primary education advisors; -Creating and providing teaching and learning materials to schools;-Coaching of teachers; -Advocacy for an improved policy environment for the teaching of reading; and -Community participation in the promotion of reading. Activities will result in improved early grade reading instruction for up to 16,000 teachers and will directly contribute to Goal 1 of the USAID Global Education Strategy by improving reading skills for more than 800,000 students in Malawi.

Objectives for Malawi: Implemented by RTI International in 11 education districts, EGRA provides technical assistance to the MoEST to improve the reading performance of Malawian students in Standards 1–3. EGRA improves early grade reading instruction, provides teaching and learning materials, encourages greater parental and community engagement in providing reading support, and strengthens the policy environment for early grade reading.

Develop and conduct needs assessments, baseline studies, targeted evaluations, special studies or other information-gathering efforts specifically for the design, monitoring and evaluation of USG-funded programs. description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Health Communication for Life activity provides technical assistance to the Malawi Ministry of Health to design and implement social and behavior change strategies to increase positive healthy behaviors among Malawians. This activity will enable the Ministry to lead national social behavior change communication programming and will coordinate key USAID implementing partners in support of national efforts. In close coordination with the Ministry of Health, the activity conducts key health communication interventions to increase positive behaviors to combat malaria and improve maternal, neonatal, and child health; promote voluntary family planning and reproductive healthcare; reinforce preventive nutrition; and improve water, sanitation and hygiene practices. This activity will target socio-cultural practices that impede adoption of good health-seeking practices and behaviors using multi-channel social behavior change communication interventions including: (1) enhancing the capacity of Ministry staff; (2) scaling up the development of locally adapted and evidence-based social behavior change interventions to reach poor, marginalized, and vulnerable people (including adolescents and youth), to prevent diseases and foster positive health practices; and, (3) promoting open dialogue on gender dynamics among adolescents and mothers, including the involvement of male champions. By increasing health-seeking behaviors, the activity contributes to the accomplishment of the U.S. President's Malaria Initiative objectives and the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.1 which seeks to improve social development..

title.narrative: USAID/Malawi’s Organized Network of Services for Everyone’s Health (ONSE) activity

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Organized Network of Services for Everyone's Health's (ONSE) activity focuses on maternal, neonatal, and child health; voluntary family planning; malaria; water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH); and nutrition. ONSE will continue to: 1) scale up effective, equitable, locally adapted, and evidence-based interventions to reach poor, marginalized, and vulnerable people, including youth and adolescents; 2) advance quality of priority health services; 3) address gender-based violence through community sensitization and awareness, one stop centres, and enhanced service for victims; and, 4) support sustainable access to WASH services and products. WASH services include supporting community and health facility driven efforts; championing the adoption of positive hygienic behaviours; and providing WASH governance bodies with skills-based training to improve the sustainable management of WASH services. Community mobilization efforts include social and behavior change communication on voluntary family planning, gender norms, timely care seeking, and healthy household practices and behaviors. ..The activity aligns with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 3.2 - Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and are able to contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work...

FY 2015 activities include:-In-service training for teachers, head teachers, and primary education advisors; -Coaching of teachers; and -Community participation in the promotion of reading. Activities will result in improved early grade reading instruction for teachers and will directly contribute to Goal 1 of the USAID Global Education Strategy by improving reading skills for students in three education districts in Malawi.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Malawi Agriculture Diversification (AgDiv)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Agriculture Diversification (AgDiv) activity promotes agricultural production, nutrition, resilience, and economic growth by helping farmers diversify away from maize into more profitable and nutritious crops, including legumes and orange-fleshed sweet potato. AgDiv will provide technical assistance, training, new technologies, demonstration plots, and media campaigns to support farmer adoption of improved technologies and practices and to improve partnerships among farmers, buyers, input suppliers, and financiers. AgDiv will use FY 2020 funds to: (1) build resilience through watershed management, reduce deforestation, and increase adoption of drip irrigation; (2) increase access to markets and finance; (3) strengthen capacity of private enterprises; (4) stimulate entrepreneurship; (5) increase productivity of legumes and orange-fleshed sweet potatoes; (6) promote good nutrition and gender related behavior change such as women empowerment; (7) and enhance resilience to shocks. .Diversification away from low-value, low-nutrient maize into legumes and orange-fleshed sweet potato will help farmers improve their dietary diversity, increase their incomes, and boost their resilience, thereby contributing to reductions in rural stunting and poverty. AgDiv partners with the private sector to implement many of its interventions, strengthening links along value chains and ensuring sustainability. .Reducing poverty, improving nutrition, and enhancing resilience to shocks are vital to achieving the Malawi Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.2 - Increase sustainable livelihoods. Increased resilience to shocks will also reduce Malawi's chronic dependence on humanitarian assistance. Further, this activity will help Malawi achieve its National Security Strategy objectives of supporting growth by unlocking the economic potential of citizens, advancing private sector interests, mobilizing private sector resources, and capitalizing on new technologies...

(Malawi): USAID/Malawi's Strengthening Evidence Based Agriculture Policy (SEBAP) activity supports capacity building efforts for the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MoAFS) to promote and increase evidence-based decision making.FY 2014 activities include: -Upgrading MoAFS's capacity to collect and aggregate data for their annual crop estimates. -Supporting monitoring and evaluation efforts of Malawi's Country Investment Plan, known as the Agriculture Sector Wide Approach.-Conducting policy analysis of key Government of Malawi agriculture policies.Activities will result in growth of the agriculture sector through improved capacity of the MoAFS to generate, analyze, and utilize accurate and reliable data and the timely availability of information to guide investments in Malawi's agricultural sector.

(Malawi): After two consecutive drought years in much of the country, 39 percent of Malawians require food assistance to survive the 2016-17 lean season. USAID will invest FY 2016 funds to reduce negative coping strategies in response to the drought and to increase resilience to future shocks. Activities will support improved management practices and the resilience of the agricultural sector, and may include some of the below:.-Forestry and agro-forestry activities to increase the amount of land under forestry cover and to diversify livelihoods;.-Soil and water conservation activities;.-Support for fish farming; and.-Irrigation development to increase the amount of agricultural land under irrigation..The objectives are to preserve Malawi's recent development gains and to increase its resilience against future shocks..

(Malawi): To support self-reliance and ensure democratic accountability, Malawian civil society organizations (CSOs) must have the necessary institutional capabilities to implement their work and engage effectively on public issues. STEPS is building the capacity of over 30 Malawian organizations to enhance their leadership and strategic management, financial management and fundraising, human resources, program management, and communications so they can deliver quality services and advocate for their constituencies. The Joint Strategic Plan notes that working with civil society groups is an important part of promoting healthy, educated, productive populations and of mobilizing support and resources to shape foreign public opinion. ..With FY18 funds, STEPS will complete training and mentoring activities to address CSO organizational needs identified through the annual capacity assessment process. This will include improving board governance and oversight, financial management, and strategic planning. STEPS will determine which CSOs are eligible for "graduation" and support an alumni and legacy institution that will provide free online and fee-for-service tailored training to enable continued assistance after project closure. The project will also support up to eight new CSOs which will have recently received grants through the Local works program and pair them with stronger CSOs to facilitate learning. Progress will be rigorously measured through self and external assessments. .STEPS will help Parliament improve its legislative and oversight functions. It will help establish a Parliamentary Budget Office and strengthen Parliament's research capabilities to help Members of Parliament contribute more effectively to the policy-making process and improve oversight of public finances and government business. Civil society organizations will help provide information to committees, thus advancing CSOs' advocacy and evidence-based policy. ....

description.narrative: (Malawi): .The New Alliance Policy Acceleration Support (NAPAS) activity assists the Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Water Development (MoAIWD) to implement key policy actions from Malawi's New Alliance Cooperation Framework. NAPAS supports two policy advisors who are based in MoAIWD's Department of Agriculture Planning Services to advance these policy priorities. Activities will include: .Development of the National Contract Farming Strategy;Finalization of the Fertilizer Strategy and Policy;Support for the development of a National Resilience Strategy; andCompletion of other New Alliance policy actions such as the Seed Act and the National Nutrition Policy.Activities will support overall improvement in the agriculture policy enabling environment to facilitate the New Alliance goal of increased private sector investment in agriculture...

title.narrative: Nutrition Capacity Development to Meet National Priorities

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID/Malawi's Nutrition Capacity Development to Meet National Priorities activity builds the capacity of the Government of Malawi's (GOM) nutrition program managers, academics and health care providers to plan, implement, monitor, and evaluate nutrition programs. The activity will: Provide technical support to the Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (LUANAR) in the implementation of postgraduate training; Update the nutrition content of the curricula for the College of Medicine, Kamuzu College of Nursing and the Malawi School for Health Sciences; and build the capacity of the Home Economy and Human Nutrition staff of LUANAR by linking them to U.S.-based universities and professors in nutrition and food science. Activities will result in the improved capacity of the GOM and nutrition practitioners to plan and implement nutrition interventions and contribute to reductions in under-nutrition in Malawi.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Malawi Strengthening Agriculture and Nutrition Extension Services (SANE)

description.narrative: (Malawi): Feed the Future's Strengthening Agricultural and Nutrition Extension (SANE) activity will continue to provide training and technical assistance to extension agents and lead farmers to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Malawi and private sector agribusinesses to deliver agriculture and nutrition extension services. In FY 2019, SANE will prioritize the consolidation of gains made over the past 4 years and share the model with other districts outside geographical focus in the final year of implementation. SANE will focus on: 1) rolling out the AgREACH Extension Helper, an extension service delivery accountability system, and other ICTs to help ensure quality of service delivery; 2) training and coaching of extension agents at various levels to serve as champions for sustainability of impacts and to help roll out methodologies used by SANE beyond the primary zone of influence; 3) training and coaching stakeholder panels at district and sub-district levels in standard operating procedures; and 4) building capacity in participatory extension approaches to help households derive better agricultural and nutritional outcomes. SANE will use organizational capacity assessment tools to evaluate progress made in strengthening capacities of various platforms to determine its primary focus areas. Access to quality extension services is essential for enhancing productivity and nutrition outcomes and thereby contributing to reductions in poverty and stunting. Reduced poverty and stunting will help achieve the Mission's Development Objective 2: Sustainable Livelihoods Increased. SANE will help farming communities hold extension institutions accountable and ensure they are responsive to farmers' needs; strengthening systems for leveraging private sector resources; and helping farmers to capitalize on new technologies. The activity will continue to focus on the 10 FTF districts in central and southern Malawi.. ..
