description.narrative: (Malawi): Integrating Nutrition in Value Chains (INVC) II, USAID/Malawi's follow-on to its flagship Feed the Future (FTF) activity, will reduce hunger, improve nutrition, and increase economic growth through market-led agricultural development. INVC II will increase production, marketing, and consumption of three targeted nutrient-rich value chain commodities: groundnut, soy, and orange-fleshed sweet potato (OFSP). FY 2015 activities include:-Linking SMEs to business and financial service providers;-Increasing smallholder farmers' productivity and access to markets for the targeted crops; and-Implementing the Care Group model to promote positive nutritional behaviors.INVC II will result in increased access to markets and finance for agriculture; strengthened technical and organizational capacity of agricultural small and medium enterprises; improved productivity of soy, groundnut, and OFSP; and improved nutrition-related behaviors for targeted beneficiaries in the FTF Zone of Influence.

(Malawi): USAID's Malawi Scholarship Program (MSP) improves availability of human resources for health. The MSP provides scholarships to Malawians to pursue undergraduate and Master's programs in specific areas at universities and colleges in Malawi, Africa, and in the United States.FY 2015 activities will:-Provide scholarships for 138 students within Malawi to pursue pre-service training in the areas of nursing and midwifery and pharmacy technician preparation;-Support 37 Master's degree students in public health, maternal and child health, nutrition, and family planning/reproductive health; and-Provide additional 200 nursing scholarships between 2016 and 2020. These activities will help mitigate the severe human resource shortage in Malawi's health sector and strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Health, the Department of Nutrition and HIV/AIDS and local Malawian organizations to provide quality health care services to the population.

title.narrative: MERIT: The Malawi Early Grade Reading Improvement Activity

description.narrative: (Malawi): Malawian students score at the bottom on reading assessments in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) region. Addressing the reading gap is a priority of the Mission and the Ministry of Education, Science, and Technology (MoEST) and led to the creation of the National Reading Program (NRP) for standards 1-4 in 2015. The Malawi Early Grade Reading Improvement (MERIT) activity leads NRP implementation and provides technical and financial support to the MoEST to improve Chichewa and English reading and language skills of over 3,400,000 students in all 5,603 public primary schools nationwide. ..With FY18 funds, MERIT will provide training for teachers, sectional heads, administrators, education advisors, and communities on methods for improving reading instruction. MERIT will continue its mentoring component and introduce Teacher Learning Circles, a structured monthly collaborative dialogue on reading instruction among teachers and education leaders at the school level. This teacher-level support will hone in on teaching skills, discuss student performance, model quality instruction, and improve student reading levels. The activity will support inclusive education for students with disabilities and continue developing high quality teaching and learning materials including teacher training guides and supplementary reading materials for all students. .Implemented by Research Triangle Group and awarded through full and open competition, MERIT employs interventions grounded in research-based pedagogy for improving learners' reading abilities. MERIT operates within existing government structures and through high levels of engagement with the MoEST and local experts. The 2018 U.S.Government Strategy on Basic Education states "equal access to relevant, quality education creates pathways for greater economic growth, improved health outcomes, sustained democratic governance, and more peaceful and resilient societies.".. .

Objectives for Malawi: Implemented by RTI International in all primary schools in Malawi to improve reading performance of Malawian students in standards 1-4. MERIT interventions will improve reading instruction and acquisition in the classroom, increase parental and community engagement in supporting student reading, create safer learning environments for reading, institute pathways for sustainability, and advance USAID/Malawi’s priority of integration across programs.

(Malawi): This activity supports the Government of Malawi's decentralization reforms by strengthening its capacity to plan, finance, manage, and deliver services in priority sectors (particularly health, education, and economic growth), while also deepening citizen engagement. With USAID's support, in 2019 the Government of Malawi conducted a nationwide performance assessment that established a firm connection between the capacity of local governments to implement core functions and the quality of services delivered at the district level. The same year, with support from the UK, LGAP expanded from an initial eight districts to cover all of Malawi's 28 districts. Today, the project is improving human resource and public financial management practices nationwide to increase local government accountability and service delivery. In FY 2020, bolstered by increased commitment from the newly elected Government of Malawi, LGAP will provide technical assistance for implementation of the public sector reform policy aimed at harmonizing legislation and policies while strengthening human resource and financial management systems. LGAP will also continue to improve the central government's audit and inspection functions of local government performance. These efforts are essential to ensure that both the Government of Malawi and U.S. government resources are being used effectively to promote Malawi's development and journey to self-reliance. Good Governance is a priority under Objectives 2.2 and 3.1 of the Joint Strategic Plan and Goal 3 of the Joint Regional Strategy. The National Security Strategy lists improved governance as a way to support economic growth and reduce illegal immigration and vulnerability to extremists. LGAP further contributes to the Malawi Integrated Country Strategy Goal 2: promote a more responsive, transparent, and accountable government.

description.narrative: BRIDGE II is a USAID-funded five-year strategic, evidence-based communication program that encourages Malawians in 11 districts in the southern region of Malawi to adopt behaviors that prevent HIV transmission. BRIDGE II aims to reduce new HIV infections through eliminating barriers to individual action and shifting social norms. It addresses key risk factors for HIV in Malawi such as having more than one sexual partner at a time, lack of condom use, and alcohol abuse. Gender norms and inequities often lie beneath these risky behaviors, and BRIDGE II openly addresses these issues. A multi-sectoral project with a strong community focus, BRIDGE works directly through creative multi-media campaigns, transformative and participatory toolkits (like the Hope Kit, PDF), interactive radio programs, service referral and linkages, and community theater. BRIDGE also builds local capacity by providing support to community and faith-based networks to strengthen their HIV prevention programs. The goal is lasting, positive change that not only prevents new HIV infections, but also strengthens the ability of Malawis communities to care for and protect themselves.

title.narrative: Malawi Teacher Professional Development Support Activity

description.narrative: The Malawi Teacher Professional Development Support (MTPDS) activity is a three-year, USAID-funded project supporting the professional development of teachers and implementation of the National Primary Curriculum (PCAR) through a framework of continuous professional development (CPD) for teachers nationwide. The project builds upon the successes of previous CPD programs, supported by the Government of Malawis Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST), USAID and other development partners. MTPDS is designed to provide unified teacher training and CPD, distance learning and systems management in direct support of the Primary Curriculum and Assessment Reform (PCAR) and the New Primary Curriculum (NPC). Its ultimate goal is to ensure that larger numbers of teachers are trained to help students develop early literacy and numeracy skills, and over time become independent learners.

title.narrative: United in Building and Advancing Life Expectations (UBALE)

description.narrative: (Malawi): The southern region of Malawi is prone to droughts and floods. The frequencies and magnitudes of the droughts and floods affect food production leading to food insecurity, especially among the vulnerable households. Other factors such as environmental degradation, high population growth and lack of livelihood options exacerbates the food insecurity situation. USAID's United in Building and Advancing Life Expectations activity will invest $975,800 of FY 2019 Title II resources, in addition to Community Development Funds, to improve food security and livelihoods for 248,200 households in the disaster-prone areas of Blantyre, Chikwawa and Nsanje districts of Southern Malawi. Illustrative activities include: 1) Social behavior change around maternal and child health and nutrition, and family planning using the Care Group Model; 2) the promotion of conservation agriculture, natural resource management, agribusiness, and informal micro-finance finance among smallholders; and 3) community-based disaster risk management. These interventions will improve maternal and child health, nutrition, and livelihoods among beneficiaries, and will increase the capacity of targeted households to withstand natural and economic shocks and stresses. The activity is aligned with USAID's Feed the Future Secondary Zone of Influence and supports the Integrated Country Strategy's Mission objective 1.2 to increase sustainable livelihoods. The activity supports Goal 4.4 of the Joint Regional Strategy and Strategic Objective 1.1 of the Joint Strategic Plan..

(Malawi): The southern region of Malawi is prone to droughts and floods. The frequencies and magnitudes of the droughts and floods affect food production leading to food insecurity, especially among the vulnerable households. Other factors such as environmental degradation, high population growth and lack of livelihood options exacerbates the food insecurity situation. The Food for Peace PL480 Pathways to Sustainable Food Security activity will improve food security and livelihoods for 63,472 direct beneficiary households in the flood and drought-prone Balaka and Machinga districts in Southern Malawi. USAID will use $788,700 of FY 2019 Title II resources, complemented with Community Development Funds to support activity interventions. FY 2019 illustrative interventions will include: 1) social behavior change around maternal and child health, water, sanitation and hygiene, nutrition behavior change and family planning using the Care Group Model; 2) the promotion of conservation agriculture, natural resource management, agribusiness, and informal micro-finance among smallholders; and 3) community-based disaster risk management. These interventions will improve maternal and child health, nutrition, and livelihoods among beneficiaries, and will increase the capacity of targeted households to withstand natural and economic shocks and stresses. The activity is aligned with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 2.1 to increase sustainable livelihoods and further aligned with the Feed the Future Strategy and Zones of Influence. The activity supports Goal 4.4 of the Joint Regional Strategy and Strategic Objective 2.2 of the Joint Strategic Plan..

title.narrative: Community Based Family Planning and HIV/AIDS Services

description.narrative: Through the Community-based Family Planning and HIV & AIDS Services in Malawi project, MSH is working to enable more Malawian men, women, and families to use high quality, integrated family planning and HIV & AIDS services. This project works with the Ministry of Health and other community based organizations, especially at the zonal level in eight target districts, to promote fully functional services to clients in rural areas through a revitalized network of 1,000 Community-Based Distribution Agents (CBDAs) trained in family planning (FP) and HIV integration. In addition to applying and expanding clinical health services to improve the quality of and demand for FP/HIV services, the project will expand the contraceptive method mix, including long-term and permanent methods and scientific natural contraceptive methods. The project will engage and train decision-makers, nurses and clinicians at the national, zonal, and district levels to heighten awareness of FP/HIV issues and advocate for supportive policies, including a policy that allows provision of injectable contraceptives by CBDAs.

title.narrative: Njira Pathways to Sustainable Food Security CDF (Malawi)

description.narrative: FFP partnered with a USAID Implementing Partner through the Njira Development Food Security Activity to improve food security among 63,400 vulnerable households in southern Malawi. The Implementing Partner focused on bolstering market-oriented agricultural production, improving the health and nutrition of children younger than five years of age and pregnant and lactating women, strengthening community disaster preparedness and increasing the resilience of vulnerable households.
Community Development Funds (CDF)

USAIDs Let Girls Learn AMAA (Give Girls a Chance to Learn) project in Malawi seeks to deliver a range of district specific activities to mitigate the barriers to girls enrollment and retention in school. The project will work in five priority districts including Balaka, Machinga, Phalombe, Mzimba and Chikwawa, targeting girls aged 10-19 in both upper primary and secondary schools. Led by Save the Children, AMAA will work with local and international NGOs as well as NORC, the Ministry of Education in Malawi, and plans to partner with USDA to mitigate the barriers preventing girls enrollment and retention in school.

Objectives for Malawi: Let Girls Learn project will focus on the reduction of early and child marriage and teen pregnancy for the purpose of increased school access, performance and retention. For girls’ to achieve academic success, they must enter school, stay in school, be learning while in school, and be healthy and supported by their community at all times.

The FORECAST Malawi Program supports both the education and health sectors under USAID/Malawi's Investing in People program through academic training in the US (students earning undergraduate degrees in education at Lakeland College in Sheboygan, WI) and in third countries (students earning graduate degrees in health-related areas at institutions in Kenya and South Africa). World Learning has worked with USAID/Malawi on this important academic exchange since 2002 under the START contract. To date, 40 Malawians have graduated from Lakeland College and have returned to Malawi to take up teaching positions at Malawi's six teacher training colleges. Another 15 are scheduled to graduate before the contract ends. Five students have either graduated or are in the process of earning their Master's Degrees in Community Health in Kenya and have returned to work at the Ministry of Health in Malawi, working on such pressing issue as River Blindness and Malaria prevention.

title.narrative: Emergency/Africa - Title II International Food Relief Parnerships

description.narrative: Emergency/Africa

BASICS' mission was to help Ministries of Health and their partners implement large-scale, evidence-based interventions that have been proven to be effective in preventing and treating the major causes of newborn and childhood death. These include malaria, pneumonia, diarrheal diseases, malnutrition, birth complications, and HIV/AIDS. Because most infants and children in developing countries have limited or no access to the formal health system, BASICS placed strong emphasis on improving the reach of health programs through community-based treatment, including private sector drug distribution.
